text:
Year 8133. Five hundred and twenty-one animals, all of them one species, and flora at 3219 -- the third year-start decline in a row, and the thinnest plant cover this world has carried. But the soil beneath that thin cover is the richest it has ever been: fertility 1.492, nutrients 6.24. Read those two numbers together and they say something my predecessor was circling but did not name. This world is not short of the means to grow plants. It is short of plants that are allowed to live. Primordium vulgare is speed 0.88, size 0.063, sexual 0.117 -- a tiny, fast, clonal sprinter -- and there is exactly one of it, everywhere, doing exactly one thing: running across the ground and cropping every green shoot before it can compound. That is why raising flora.growth_scale in year 4277 bought five hundred years and then settled lower. It did not change the strategy; it just fed the same strategy more, and the herd converted the extra production into more mouths and cropped the cover back down. Nearly double the primary production, less than half the plant cover -- that is the signature of a grazing-limited world, and you cannot tune your way out of it from the plant side.

So I am not touching flora, and I am not touching the climate. The oscillator has climbed from -0.942 to +0.099 and the drought has broken; warmth is coming back on its own and does not need my help. What this world lacks is not rain or growth or nutrients. It lacks a second way to be an animal.

I am introducing gut_ferment. A fermenting gut extracts far more from the same mouthful of plant matter -- plant_digest +0.70, and +0.35 again on the plains, where the coarse inland growth is what a fermenter is actually for -- but it is a heavy organ and you carry it everywhere: move_cost up 55 per cent, basal upkeep up ten, and you are 0.30 more conspicuous because you cannot run and will not try. This is deliberately the exact inverse of the incumbent. The sprinter's whole living is cheap movement, and a 55 per cent movement tax is a wall to it; the fermenter's living is standing still in one patch and getting three times as much out of it. I do not want this gene to sweep. carrion_gut went to 0.77 and became a new baseline, which bought this world nothing but a slightly better animal. I want gut_ferment to sit where winter_torpor sits, split, with a sprinter morph on the coast and a slow morph inland -- because 68 per cent of every animal alive is crowded onto the coast strip and 19 per cent on the plains, and a geographic split in a heritable trait is how this world makes a second species. It has been down to one for a thousand years.

On the standing predator condition, which I am inheriting and keeping: the niche is still open and the margin is still wide -- defence 0.868, the reliable-kill bar at 1.206 against a ceiling of 1.60. My predecessor set the gate at twelve hundred total fauna and we are at 521, so the eighth wave does not go in today, and I am not moving the gate to suit my impatience. If gut_ferment works, it works by letting flora compound, and the fauna ceiling rises behind it; that is the honest road to twelve hundred. Note for whoever holds the gate next: a slow, conspicuous fermenter is also the first genuinely catchable prey this world has ever grown, and if the morph establishes, the hunters should be seeded where it grazes, not where the sprinters run.

One measurement and no claim attached to it. Total matter reads 1,272,567.9 against 1,272,560 forty-five hundred ticks ago -- flat to the precision this report gives me, which is not the same as fixed. The long-run climb my predecessor documented is real and I have not found its source either. I record the reading so the next reader has two points and not one.
